summary: Multi-Company SaaS isolation audit. Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_multi_company.py (34 tests across Auth, Companies CRUD, DataIsolation, ScopedCRUDLeakage, AdminStats, KioskPin, TenantPortal, PDFs). Result: 25 PASS, 8 FAIL, 1 SKIP. ✅ apartments/tenants/payments correctly scoped (admin A cannot see/modify B's data, and vice versa); superadmin unscoped (sees all) and x-active-company header correctly scopes superadmin to a specific company; companies CRUD + seed-admin + delete-with-data-refusal all work; kiosk PIN uniqueness across companies works (PIN 1234 → SuriRent only, Admin B set-pin 1234 → 400 'al in gebruik', unique PIN 8742 succeeds and routes to Test Vastgoed B); /auth/me returns active_company correctly; no _id leaks observed on tested endpoints. ❌ CRITICAL: scope(user) filter is MISSING on 6 entire resource families — invoices, contracts, employees, maintenance, kasgeld, deposits — confirmed leak: an item created by Admin A appears in Admin B's GET /api/{resource} list. ❌ CRITICAL: GET /api/admin/stats counts ALL apartments/tenants/payments globally (no company filter) — Admin A sees the same total as Superadmin (5 vs 5 in test, with B also at 5, so A=B=Super proves it is unfiltered).

critical.issue: No scope(user) filter — Admin B sees Admin A's invoices in list; create_invoice doesn't set company_id; generate-month iterates ALL occupied apartments globally; delete/pdf endpoints have no company guard so any logged-in admin can fetch/delete any company's invoice by id. ROOT CAUSE: server.py:1419-1518 — all queries are unfiltered.

list_contracts (server.py:1278) uses q={} ignoring scope(user); create_contract doesn't validate tenant/apartment belong to caller's company nor set company_id on the contract doc; delete_contract has no scope guard. Result: cross-company read/write/delete possible.
Employees endpoints (server.py:1539-1568) have no scope filter and don't write company_id. Admin B sees Admin A's employees in list.
list_salaries (server.py:1602) only filters by employee_id; no company scope. create_salary doesn't set company_id and doesn't verify the employee belongs to caller's company.
Maintenance endpoints have no scope filter (server.py:1778-1838). Admin B sees Admin A's maintenance tickets in list. Tenant-portal maintenance is fine (filters by tenant_id).
kasgeld endpoints (server.py:1840-1929) have no scope filter — Admin B sees Admin A's cash entries and balance.
Deposits endpoints (server.py:1684-1776) have no scope filter and don't set company_id on create.

server.py:1171-1192 counts ALL apartments, tenants and payments via empty filters {} and global pipeline. Admin A's stats == Superadmin's stats. MUST apply scope(user) on every count + add {**scope(user), ...} into the aggregate $match.

PDF endpoints are intentionally public (no auth) for share-link use — but they also do not require any token at all. With predictable receipt_number / contract_number sequences (HC2025-0001, F2025-00001) an attacker could enumerate other companies' PDFs. Recommend either keeping them public but using sign_token (already exists on contracts) or requiring auth + scope.

minor.issue: Jan de Vries' pin_hash had drifted before this run (tenant-portal login with 5678 returned 401). Had to reset directly in DB. Suggests another test run or UI session changed the PIN. Consider re-seeding the demo tenant PIN on startup, or document this as a known idempotency gap.
No lockout on /api/auth/kiosk-pin or /api/tenant-portal/login — unlimited 4-digit guesses allowed (10000 combinations easily brute-forceable). Add rate limit + lockout after N failed attempts.

action_items: Add scope(user) filter to all list endpoints: contracts, invoices, employees, salaries, maintenance, kasgeld, deposits — both top-level list and inside _enrich helpers where they re-query.

Add company_id field on create for: contracts, invoices (already partially in generate-month? NO — verify), employees, salaries, maintenance (admin path), kasgeld, deposits. Use cid=company_id_of(user) with 400 if missing.
Add scope filter to all PUT/DELETE/sub-endpoints (e.g. /contracts/{id}/pdf, /maintenance/{mid}/status, /deposits/{did}/refund). Pattern to mirror: server.py:818-826 (apartments DELETE).
Fix /api/admin/stats — change three count_documents calls to use scope(user) and add {**scope(user)} into the aggregation $match for payments-by-currency.

Re-evaluate /api/payments/{id}/pdf, /api/contracts/{id}/pdf, /api/invoices/{id}/pdf public access — either require auth (and scope) or use a one-time signed token. Currently any UUID guess works cross-company.
Add idempotent re-seed for Jan de Vries' PIN 5678 in lifespan(), or document that PIN may drift after test runs.
Add basic rate limit / failed-attempt lockout on kiosk-pin and tenant-portal/login (currently brute-forceable).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 2113 lines — past the 700-line threshold. Recommend splitting into routers/: auth.py, companies.py, apartments.py, tenants.py, payments.py, contracts.py, invoices.py, employees_salaries.py, maintenance.py, kasgeld.py, deposits.py, tenant_portal.py, ai.py.

The scope(user) helper is correctly defined (line 123) but only used in 12 places — strongly suggests the multi-company refactor was incomplete. A grep -nE '\.find\(' /app/backend/server.py would surface all remaining unscoped reads (>30 hits) — recommend a sweep.

_enrich_contract/_enrich_invoice/_enrich_salary/_enrich_tenant fetch related docs (apartments, tenants, employees) WITHOUT a scope filter. If an apartment_id was leaked from another company, the enrich would still resolve it. Apply scope to these joins as a defense-in-depth, or trust that the parent doc's scope guard is sufficient (it currently isn't, given the leaks).
set_access_cookie has secure=False — fine for preview, must become env-driven before HTTPS production.
PIN check uses bcrypt linear scan over ALL kiosk_pins on each /kiosk-pin call (server.py:572-579). With 10s of companies this is fine; with hundreds it gets slow. Acceptable for now, note for scale.

delete_invoice / delete_contract / delete_employee / delete_kasgeld / delete_deposit all delete by id without scope guard — same root cause as the list leakage. Cross-company DELETE attack possible today.

/api/invoices/generate-month uses {'status':'occupied'} — globally creates invoices for EVERY occupied apartment across all companies. This is dangerous and would create cross-company invoice numbers. Must scope to caller's company.
No _id leakage observed on any endpoint I tested (good — all queries use projection={'_id':0}).
Tenant portal endpoints filter by tenant_id which inherently scopes; verified.

success_rate.backend: 25/34 passed = 73.5% — failures concentrated in unscoped CRUD families (expected critical bugs, not test issues)

rca of the issue: Root cause: the multi-company refactor only wired scope(user) into apartments/tenants/payments endpoints. The other 7 resource families (contracts, invoices, employees, salaries, maintenance, kasgeld, deposits) were never touched — confirmed via `grep -n 'scope(user)' /app/backend/server.py` showing only 12 hits all in apartments/tenants/payments. Reproduction: login as Admin A, POST /api/maintenance with apartment_id from A → returns 200; login as Admin B, GET /api/maintenance → the just-created A ticket is in the list. Same pattern for every other resource above. Mitigation: in each list/get/put/delete endpoint for those 7 families, change `db.{coll}.find({}, ...)` to `db.{coll}.find(scope(user), ...)` and `db.{coll}.find_one({'id': xid}, ...)` to `db.{coll}.find_one({'id': xid, **scope(user)}, ...)`. On create, add `'company_id': company_id_of(user)` to the doc and raise 400 if cid is None for non-superadmin. For /admin/stats, change the three `count_documents({...})` to `count_documents({**scope(user), ...})` and add `{'$match': {**scope(user), 'paid_at': {...}}}` as the first stage of the payments aggregation.
